title: Jump risk premia in the presence of clustered jumps

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs a bivariate Hawkes process option pricing model to capture self- and cross-exciting positive and negative jumps in cryptocurrency markets. A two-stage calibration is employed: first, model parameters under the physical P-measure are estimated using historical Bitcoin price data via a Peak-Over-Threshold (POT) jump filter and maximum likelihood estimation; second, risk-premia parameters under the risk-neutral Q-measure are calibrated to market implied volatilities. The resulting jump risk premia are then tested for their predictive power on the cost-of-carry in Bitcoin futures and the returns of delta-hedged option strategies.
extraction.universe: Bitcoin (BTC) spot prices, one-month BTC futures, and BTC options traded on Deribit

performance_metrics.context: Regression of BTC futures basis c_t on jump risk premia (Regression I)
Comprehensive regression of BTC futures basis c_t including jump risk premia, jump counts, and funding rates (Regression VI)
Regression of one-week-ahead portfolio returns for the straddle option strategy

key_findings: The bivariate Hawkes process effectively captures clustered positive and negative jumps, generating asymmetric, time-varying implied volatility skews in Bitcoin options.
Jump risk premia exhibit significant explanatory power for the cost-of-carry in Bitcoin futures, achieving an adjusted R2 of up to 31% when combined with jump counts and funding rates.
Inferred jump risk premia forecast one-week-ahead returns of delta-hedged option portfolios, confirming that systematic option selling strategies can capture these risk premia.
limitations: The model assumes that the risk-premium parameters are constant for the specification of model dynamics.
